sentences.text: This meeting is being recorded.
Hey, Trent, how you doing?
I'm good.
How are you?
Yeah, I'm good, thank you.
Whereabouts are you based?
Denver.
Denver, Colorado.
How about yourself?
Weird going on in Denver at the moment.
Everybody is in Denver.
Is that right?
Do you know what, every day this week and last week, I've had a call to somebody in Denver.
Don't know what's going on.
It's the center of the universe for marketing agencies right now.
That's good to hear.
We'll see if we, we can.
We need to buy some of them then.
We, we don't own anything in Denver.
We've, we've been here.
Mountain Gates operated out of Denver for 25 years and we, we've only owned one company actually headquartered here.
We just bought.
Oh because we work on the buy side as well.
We just bought a company called Hovercraft which is based in Denver.
It's beautiful business.
Fantastic.
Doing really well as well under new ownership.
So all good.
Awesome.
Well, great to connect.
I don't know if we've met before.
Our firms have worked together before.
But we've connected with Monica a bunch over the years.
So when she makes an introduction, we always love to touch base and say hello and see what we can do to find a path together.
Yeah, brilliant.
So you're interested in one of the businesses we've got listed at the moment, which is I think the New York one.
I guess.
To be perfectly honest, I don't.
The only context that I have is Monica sending us an email saying, hey Trent, I think you would be interested in this business.
You should talk to Andy.
And so which is great because I've only probably.
I talked to Monica about three times in my life and it was probably about three years ago, so it was an out of the blue referral.
But obviously she knows what you're looking for.
I guess that was great.
So, I mean, be good to get some context on what you guys are doing.
I've looked on your website and I can see, I think you're doing 5 to 25 million EBITDA platforms.
And then I guess you're just looking at bolt ons for the business that you've already acquired.
Yeah, I think that's a fair statement.
I mean we as a firm just closed out investing out of our second fund, which was a $475 million fund.
We just raised a $570 million fund, so about $100 million more.
We closed that fund in January and now we did our last two deals in fund two in Q1.
And so we're hitting the road now looking for new platforms.
So I think 5 to 25 is probably the appropriate band.
We probably have a little bit of flexibility on either end to do that.
We're generally looking to write an initial equity investment.
You know, 30 would be on the very low end.
60, you know, is kind of maybe the, the higher end of what would be an appropriate kind of first bite platform equity check investment.
And then we're maybe looking to, you know, add another 10 or $15 million of equity by doing add ons over the course of our hold period.
We're not a super acquisitive firm in the sense that we don't do roll ups.
We, we do, but when we talk about buy and build we say, we set out and say, hey, what are we doing?
We're all B2B services.
That's 100% of what we do.
So if we're doing a service for a big enterprise, what are the three adjacent services that are highest value, highest cross sell, highest impact to the customer, retention and sustainability.
And we try to add those and then invest in some technology to wrap it all around together.
And that's generally been the model that we've operated with.
We tend to partner primarily with founder owned businesses both on the platform and the add on.
We're not opposed to doing a non founder owned business but it's definitely been, you know, our, our primary strike zone.
And so we certainly have a bunch of, you know, and then in particular underneath that there's a bunch of marketing services investments that we've made over time.
So While everything is B2B, probably half of our portfolio is in the marketing services realm specifically.
And that's what I spend 100% of my time on.
So the interaction that I've had with Monica over the years has been talking about Market Smith and you know, kind of, you know, our potential interest in it over the years.

And so yeah, I haven't spoke to her, you know, in probably over a year and then I got the email so I wasn't sure if the, the subtle suggestion was that the company that she was referencing was Market Smith or if, or if there was some other, you know, kind of strong capability.
But I know we're in the process of executing the NDA so we'll take a look at it and happy to circle back, you know, on it after we.
Yeah, that is a bit strange.
I don't know what her insight connect is.
Funny.
I'm happy that she did well.

Yeah, no, I mean you know, look, I mean something kind of roughly like you called out, you know, 30, 30 of revenue, 1 of EBITDA, you know, it probably feels like a good add on opportunity for one of our platforms.
And so, you know, we'll, we'll definitely take a look and kind of express interest.

But I mean in general, to the extent that you guys, you know, would be fantastic just to get in your CRM and make sure that we're seeing deals from you guys as you have opportunities that are, you know.
Yeah, well, you're in there now for sure.
So Monica, I was going to say.
Based on this opportunity alone, certainly like the stuff that you guys are working on is probably broadly in our wheelhouse.
And you know, again, to the extent that it's more on the B2B side as opposed to consumer side.
Yeah, well, it's definitely in your wheelhouse, Trent, if you're working 100 on the, the 50 of your portfolio that is marketing services.
So 100 of what we're doing is marketing services.
Oh, there you go.
So definitely we've got the platform Agencies co.
We're capital A group, but we have agencies co, which is where we list our marketing agency businesses.
So definitely good to get you on the mailing list for that and we'll send you more opportunities as they come.
And then in our CRM.
Yeah, we just make sure that we're sending you appropriate sizes.
Yeah, that's great.
Yeah.
Again, I would say that like everything I quoted is for platforms.
Obviously add ons kind of have no minimum.
Yeah.
You know, so you know, I'd say and you know, look, we probably have seven or eight, you know, platform companies and marketing services right now.
So almost anything in the marketing services realm probably fits potentially with one of them.
And so certainly, you know, we probably have a pretty wide aperture of what we would take a look at and kick the tires on and potentially find a home for.
Okay, well that's everything on our website potentially.
But so I mean, do you want to give us a.
Where are your hotspots, you know, at the moment?
Because we are talking probably to about 100, 150 agencies a month.
Very good.
Yeah.

So I'd say the platforms of ours that are probably the most acquisitive right now are first one, I'll mention, bond brand loyalty and they would primarily be looking for a like Salesforce, email CRM, customer experience management and communication shop.
That's probably the biggest area that they're most interested in.
They have some good creative capabilities and strategy capabilities and they have A loyalty management platform.
But they're really missing that communication piece where they're doing the ongoing, you know, consumer outreach for their clients.
The second one would be Ignite Visibility.
Ignite Visibility is really focused on franchise and multi unit businesses as their core clients.
So they do everything from local marketing, website build and management and paid media primarily for what we would say is natural national to local businesses.
And so you know, for them, you know, again it's kind of really more about the somebody who focuses on that end client base.
So we've got a Legion company that's focused on franchisees.
So that could be a good fit.
Yeah, certainly could be a, could be an interesting one to chat about.
So yeah, something like that could be a good fit like Legion and then again kind of the same life cycle management ecosystem, email CRM capability for them, but more focused on that broad base.
Anything, you know, if it's, if it's relatively small, we don't obviously want to buy a big thing.
But like kind of direct mail management, you know, kind of anything that drives like kind of more local awareness is kind of what's key for that business.
Right.
So we drive pretty bright line between e commerce businesses where it's all about finding the right consumer for the right brand.
But anywhere on the Internet because you can drop ship them a product.

And what these guys are doing is all of their clients are like home services, auto services, healthcare services, where it's entirely about making sure that either you have the awareness of oh shit, I saw a flyer for that dental practice, I should go check it out.
Or when somebody says shit, I need a dentist and they type into Google like you know, dentists near me that you know, our clients show up on top of that list.
So it's kind of more about discoverability than it is awareness.
But obviously if you get the discoverability down then the awareness can be a big powerful component.
And so the direct mail tends to be a big advertising component for those local businesses.
Not in the direct mail space so much but certainly performance marketing is definitely.
That could work too.
A lot of those types of things.
Okay, so we've got this New York performance marketing company and we've got the franchisee one which is 1.4 million EBITDA.
So there's a couple of businesses that might be the right kind of size for you in terms of bolt ons that should work.
Yeah, cool.
Something like that would be great to take a look at.
And so that, that sounds, that sounds fantastic.
So yeah, no, well look, fantastic to meet you.
I'LL have to circle back at some point to ask Monica what, what it was about that opportunity, you know, that, that spurned the introduction.

But it sounds, regardless, it actually, regardless of that specific opportunity, it sounds like this was a, a really good introduction because obviously we're swimming in all the same lanes and so look forward to seeing more outreach from you guys and, and seeing some deal flow and obviously happy to connect and compare notes on the space as we go forward here.
Yeah, fantastic.
Fantastic.
Yeah, I mean, I am always calling Denver so.
Well, next time you come through, drop me a line and we can grab a coffee or something.
Yeah, I think, I think I need to pay a visit for sure.
Yeah.
A very good friend of mine just lives just outside of Denver and I mean he is talking up that place.
He's talking about it all the time.
So I mean, it seems to me it's fantastic.
It's.
Yeah, I've, I moved here first in 2010, lived here for a few years and then lived in New York for six and then moved back in like 2018.
And so I've been back since and it's, it's great.
It's a fantastic place to raise a family.
You're.
The mountains are right here.
So I'd say you've got that lifestyle thing.
You say you've got the urban center and all this sort of cool stuff going on, but you're just.
Yeah, I mean, I'd say so.
I'd say Denver.
Yeah.
So Denver, the city is now big enough that it actually supports enough infrastructure that like you have, you know, some proper restaurants and nightlife and things.
You're not like living in Omaha, right?
Yeah.
But at the same time, you're right, you're only 30 minutes from the mountains and you know, some kind of world class hiking or skiing or camping or fishing, whatever you do.

And then to cap it off, I think that weather is probably the best kept secret because it's, you know, 300 days of sunshine, you know, crystal clear skies most days, you know, pretty temperate weather.
So.
Yeah, no, I, I could, I could give the pitch on it.
Plus, if you're, if you travel a lot like I do, it's pretty nice to deploy out of Denver because you can hit both coasts in under, you know, three and a half hours.
So it's not too bad.
Perfect.
If you find your way out, then we'd love to say hello and.
Yeah, definitely.
I think that's, it's on my, my list of places I need to get to in the next couple of months.
Absolutely.
Well, good to meet you, Trent.
Great to meet you.
I do appreciate the time.
Let's start working together.
Sounds great.
Love it.
All right, thanks.

summary.overview: The Introductory Business Development Call between Trenton Sisson of Mountain Gate Capital and Andy Day of Capital A Group/Agencies Co focused on establishing a collaborative relationship and exploring potential investment opportunities in the marketing services sector. The meeting began with introductions and overviews of both companies, highlighting Mountain Gate's recent $570 million fund and their strategic investment approach targeting founder-owned B2B services with an emphasis on high-quality add-ons. The discussion included current acquisition interests, such as technology enhancements for their platforms and specific targets like a New York performance marketing firm and a franchise-focused lead generation company. Both parties expressed a desire to build their relationship, agreed to share relevant deal flow, and highlighted the importance of connecting in person, particularly due to Denver's growing business prominence. Action items were identified, including adding contacts to CRM systems and further reviewing potential investment opportunities.
summary.short_summary: Trenton Sisson from Mountain Gate Capital and Andy Day from Capital A Group had a productive introductory call aimed at establishing a collaborative relationship and identifying potential investment opportunities in the marketing services sector. The meeting highlighted Mountain Gate's recent $570 million fund, focusing on strategic investments in founder-owned B2B services, especially high-quality add-ons. Discussions included current acquisition interests like technology enhancements for their platforms and specific targets such as a performance marketing firm located in New York and a franchise-focused lead generation company. Both participants expressed a strong desire to nurture their relationship, agreed to share relevant deal flow, and recognized the significance of in-person connections, especially given Denver's growing business prominence. Action items included integrating contacts into their CRM systems and further reviewing investment opportunities.
